variant.label: Conventional deadlift, 200 kg · contact v2 experiment

model.name: Catelli v4 marker-enabled full-body squat model (Rajagopal/Lai lineage), derived copy
transformations: loaded the byte-identical marker-enabled Catelli v4 model
set appliesForce=false on every Force in the ForceSet (80 muscles, 17 coordinate actuators) so inverse dynamics sees gravity and external loads only
no barbell body: the bar is a rigid hand-carried load applied at both palms during inverse dynamics
model.license_note: SimTK project page records an MIT use agreement; the derived model is generated locally and not redistributed.

assumptions: Shank-angle and trunk-inclination timelines are authored; straight-arm shoulder-to-palm inclination and a smooth bar path are constrained before complete inverse-dynamics recomputation. Foot closure is imposed; balance is emergent and COP must remain in the foot.
The floor pose solves the original fixed knee angle and exact plate height, full shoulder-to-palm line, and clearance of the fixed fitted leg/pelvis triangle envelope.
The motion is sagittal, bilaterally symmetric, and conventional-stance; sumo stance, toe-out, grip asymmetry, and left/right differences are not modelled.

The barbell (200 kg) is a rigid load carried at both palms with a 50/50 hand split; it is not part of the OpenSim model, its inertial and gravitational load is applied at the palms during inverse dynamics, and the bar keeps a horizontal axis.

Arms have zero elbow flexion and fixed grip abduction. The complete shoulder-to-grip line transitions smoothly from 5 degrees shoulder-ahead at setup to 12.8 degrees grip-ahead at lockout. The wrist-to-grip station is 75 mm, fitted to the human's fixed articulated hand before computing kinematics, velocities and loads. Grip strength and finger contact forces are not modelled.

Ground reaction is derived from the model's own momentum balance (Newton-Euler) including the bar and split 50/50 between the feet; the centre of pressure and vertical free moment follow from that balance.
The starting posture is the pose in which the bar centre sits one plate radius above the floor; the bar leaves the floor at the start of the pull without a separate tension-building phase.

Segment masses and inertias are the generic Catelli/Rajagopal values for a 75 kg lifter; no subject scaling was applied. Its shoulder-to-palm reach is about 0.585 m, so the start position is more horizontal than a lifter with longer arms would need.

The entire smooth authored trajectory clears the fixed fitted leg/pelvis surface. Contact calibration occurs before differentiation; there is no per-frame path push or surface deformation. The old cylinder-based shin statistic is retained for baseline comparison but does not define acceptance.
Muscles and coordinate actuators were disabled; results are net joint moments, not muscle, joint-contact, or spinal forces.
claims_boundary: Simulated lift: the kinematics are authored/solved and the external forces are model-derived, not measured. Net joint moments describe this simulation only. No muscle force, joint-contact force, spinal load, coaching, or injury-risk claim is made.

frames.axes: OpenSim ground frame: x forward (toes), y up, z to the lifter's right; body meshes and transforms share this convention

sign_notes.pelvis_tilt: positive = posterior tilt; negative = anterior tilt

bar.force_note: force the lifter must apply to the bar: m_bar * (a_bar - g); equal and opposite to the load on the lifter
bar.hand_force_note: force the bar applies to each hand (half the bar load), applied at the palm station in inverse dynamics

ground_reaction.method: Newton-Euler balance of all model bodies plus the carried bar from finite-differenced momenta at the sampled rate
ground_reaction.split_assumption: bilaterally symmetric: each foot receives half the total force at the shared centre-of-pressure x under its own midline

inverse_dynamics.method: opensim.InverseDynamicsSolver with finite-differenced speeds/accelerations; ground wrench under each calcaneus and half the bar load at each palm applied through station/frame Jacobian transposes

residuals.meaning: Generalized forces left on the six pelvis-to-ground mobilities; near zero means the kinematics, inertia, and applied loads are mutually consistent.

path_screen.note: Pass permits kinematics and net moments only; muscle, static-optimization, and joint-reaction outputs remain out of scope for this bundle.

experiment.status: local experiment, pending visual and scientific acceptance

body_contact.method: Conservative finite-shaft anterior leg/pelvis triangle-edge envelope on all serialized replay frames

experiment.method: Fixed fitted surface; full shoulder-to-palm straight-arm line; smooth progress-domain bar path and arm inclination; complete force/moment recomputation.
